concepts.name: Definition and Classification of Invasive Alien Species (IAS)
key_dimensions: Distinction between 'alien/exotic', 'naturalized', and 'invasive' species — UPSC often conflates these
CBD definition vs. IUCN definition vs. Indian legal definition under Biological Diversity Act
Difference between invasive native species and invasive alien species — a common trap
Why not all alien species become invasive — the '10s Rule' (invasion ecology)

concepts.name: Pathways and Vectors of IAS Introduction
key_dimensions: Intentional vs. unintentional introduction — examples of each (e.g., Lantana camara vs. ballast water species)
CBD COP 10 Nagoya framework classifying pathways: release, escape, contaminant, stowaway, corridor, unaided
Role of trade, tourism, and climate change in accelerating introductions
Ballast water as a major vector — IMO Ballast Water Management Convention and India's position

concepts.name: Ecological Impacts of IAS on Native Biodiversity
key_dimensions: HIPPO framework — IAS as the second leading cause of biodiversity loss globally after habitat destruction
Mechanisms: competition, predation, hybridization, disease transmission, ecosystem engineering
Island biogeography and why island ecosystems are disproportionately vulnerable
Case studies: Nile Perch in Lake Victoria, Brown Tree Snake in Guam, Lantana in Indian forests

concepts.name: IAS and Economic/Socio-cultural Impacts
key_dimensions: Global cost estimates — IPBES 2023 report pegging annual losses at $423 billion
Impact on agriculture, fisheries, forestry, and water security in India
Parthenium hysterophorus — health impacts on humans and livestock alongside ecological damage
Socio-cultural dimension: displacement of traditional livelihoods, sacred groves invasion

concepts.name: Global Governance Framework for IAS — CBD and Kunming-Montreal GBF
key_dimensions: CBD Article 8(h) — the primary international obligation to prevent, control, or eradicate IAS
Kunming-Montreal GBF Target 6: reduce introduction rate of IAS by 50% by 2030 — specific numbers matter
Distinction between Target 6 obligations vs. previous Aichi Target 9 — what changed
Relationship between CBD, CITES, and Ramsar Convention in regulating IAS

concepts.name: IPBES Assessment Report on IAS (2023)
key_dimensions: First dedicated global assessment on IAS by IPBES — key findings and their policy implications
3,500 IAS causing documented harm; 37,000 alien species established globally
Three-tier management hierarchy: prevention > early detection/rapid response > control/eradication
Report's finding on climate change as a future accelerator of IAS spread — synergistic threats

concepts.name: India's Legal and Regulatory Framework for IAS
key_dimensions: Biological Diversity Act 2002 — Section 38 on regulation of introduction of exotic species; lacunae in enforcement
Environment Protection Act 1986 as a fallback regulatory tool for IAS control
National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) vs. State Biodiversity Boards — division of IAS management responsibility
Absence of a standalone IAS legislation in India — comparison with New Zealand's Biosecurity Act

concepts.name: India's National List of Invasive Alien Species and Institutional Mechanisms
key_dimensions: Role of MoEFCC, ICAR, and ZSI/BSI in identifying and listing IAS — overlapping mandates
National Biodiversity Action Plan (NBAP) provisions on IAS
India's reporting obligations under CBD and gap between commitments and ground-level action
Quarantine laws — Plant Quarantine Order 2003 and its relationship with IAS prevention

concepts.name: Major Invasive Flora in India: Case Studies
key_dimensions: Lantana camara — origin, spread mechanism, impact on forest understorey and wildlife corridors
Parthenium hysterophorus (Congress grass) — health, agricultural, and ecological impacts; biological control attempts
Prosopis juliflora (Vilayati kikar) — paradox of being both invasive and used for livelihood/fuelwood in drylands
Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia crassipes) — aquatic ecosystem choking, impact on fisheries and wetlands

concepts.name: Major Invasive Fauna in India: Case Studies
key_dimensions: Common Carp and Tilapia — introduced for aquaculture, now threatening native freshwater fish diversity
Red-eared Slider turtle — pet trade pathway, competition with native softshell turtles
Suckermouth armored catfish (Pterygoplichthys) — invasion of rivers including Ganga tributaries
African Giant Snail (Achatina fulica) — agricultural pest and disease vector; comparison with marine invasives

concepts.name: Invasive Species in Marine and Coastal Ecosystems
key_dimensions: Ballast water introduction mechanism — Caulerpa taxifolia in Mediterranean as global reference case
Indian context: Kappaphycus alvarezii (seaweed) smothering coral reefs in Gulf of Mannar
Mangrove invasives vs. mangrove restoration — policy tension
IMO Ballast Water Management Convention 2004 — India's ratification status and implementation challenges

concepts.name: Prevention as the Most Cost-Effective IAS Strategy: Biosecurity and Border Control
key_dimensions: Economic argument: prevention costs vs. control costs ratio (IPBES data — prevention 100x cheaper)
Risk assessment tools: Weed Risk Assessment (WRA) system used in Australia — India's adoption status
CITES regulation of live specimen trade as an IAS prevention tool — overlap and gaps
Role of Customs, FSSAI, and NBPGR (National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources) in border biosecurity

concepts.name: Early Detection and Rapid Response (EDRR) Systems for IAS
key_dimensions: Concept of 'lag phase' in invasion biology — why early detection windows are missed
Citizen science platforms: iNaturalist, India Biodiversity Portal as EDRR tools
IUCN ISSG (Invasive Species Specialist Group) — global early warning role
India's lack of a functional national EDRR system — policy gap and recommendations

concepts.name: Biological Control of IAS: Methods, Successes, and Risks
key_dimensions: Classical biological control vs. augmentative vs. inundative approaches
Success case: Zygogramma bicolorata beetle for Parthenium control in India
Risk of 'biocontrol agents themselves becoming invasive' — the Cane Toad paradox in Australia
Regulatory approval process for biocontrol agents in India — RCGM and biosafety norms

concepts.name: Mechanical and Chemical Control of IAS and Their Limitations
key_dimensions: Manual removal vs. mechanical clearing — cost-effectiveness and regrowth problem
Herbicide use for IAS control — glyphosate controversy, non-target effects, soil health
Integrated Pest Management (IPM) approach combining multiple methods
Eradication vs. control vs. containment — when each strategy is appropriate based on invasion stage

concepts.name: IAS and Climate Change: The Synergy Trap
key_dimensions: Climate change expanding thermal ranges enabling IAS to colonize new habitats (e.g., alpine zones)
CO2 fertilization effect disproportionately benefiting invasive C3 plants over native species
IAS themselves contributing to climate change — Prosopis and water hyacinth altering carbon cycles
IPCC-IPBES joint report 2021 on biodiversity-climate nexus and IAS as a cross-cutting threat

concepts.name: IAS in Protected Areas: Specific Challenges
key_dimensions: Buffer zone as entry point for IAS into core protected areas — management failure
Case: Lantana invasion in Nagarhole, Corbett, and Sariska — impact on herbivore grazing and tiger habitat
Ecorestoration mandates under Wildlife Protection Act and National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) guidelines
Tension between IAS removal and carbon sequestration credits if invasive trees are counted in afforestation data

concepts.name: The Paradox of 'Useful Invasives': Policy and Ethical Dilemmas
key_dimensions: Prosopis juliflora: used for fuel, charcoal, and soil stabilization in Rajasthan — removal vs. utilization debate
Eucalyptus and Acacia plantations — commercially valuable but ecologically invasive in India
Eichhornia (water hyacinth) as biogas feedstock and handicraft material — perverse incentive to retain it
Policy contradiction: same species listed invasive by MoEFCC but promoted by state forest departments for social forestry

concepts.name: IUCN's 100 Worst Invasive Species List: India-Relevant Entries
key_dimensions: Composition of the list — criteria used (impact breadth, irreversibility, symbolic value for awareness)
India-relevant species: Common Carp, Water Hyacinth, Lantana, African Giant Snail, Rats (Rattus rattus)
Distinction: the list is awareness tool, not a binding regulatory instrument — UPSC trap
Gaps in the list — why some highly damaging species in India are not included (regional bias in data)

concepts.name: Restoration Ecology and Post-IAS Removal Ecosystem Recovery
key_dimensions: Concept of 'invasion debt' — time lag between IAS removal and ecosystem recovery
Native species reintroduction after IAS eradication — case of island restorations globally
India's Compensatory Afforestation Fund (CAMPA) and whether it funds IAS removal as ecological restoration
UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration (2021–2030) — IAS management as a restoration priority and India's commitments
